title: Succession vocabulary -- what may become of a prior system's path, declared once (ADR-011)
description: The one home of every DISPOSITION a migration map may assign to a path of a host's prior agent system. Each disposition names the fields a row assigning it must carry, and what each field REFERS to; the interpreter checks a reference by its kind and holds no disposition by name. `undecided` names the state of a path no row answers -- a declared absence that no row may assign. A new disposition is a row here, never an edit to the interpreter.

residence.description: The ONE place in a host where its migration map resides -- a host-relative path in a plane that a capability declares as an install target (seeded blank). A roster is carried out only from the map that lives here: a map passed from anywhere is a judgement with no home (ADR-012).

receives.description: The install modes whose declared SPACES may receive a relocated path. A space outside these is one whose bytes a writer of this kit rebuilds or owns, and a path moved into it would be overwritten or unaccounted.

effect.description: What carrying this disposition out does to the path, named from the interpreter's effect registry (ADR-012). Declared, never inferred from the fields a row carries: a disposition whose effect had to be guessed would be a deletion by default. A disposition that declares NO effect is readable and is never carried out: a path it answers refuses the act, because an absent effect is not a default one.

carries.description: Every field a row with this disposition must carry, and nothing else it may carry.

refers.description: The kind of thing the value names; checked by the interpreter's reference registry.
